title: Memory channel and spot market: module makers, brokers and how memory price shocks reach device makers (2019-2026)
why_it_matters: Spot prices and module makers (Kingston, ADATA and others) are the first to feel memory shortages and gluts, and the 2025-26 price spike shows memory cost now shapes PC and phone pricing. Public data on this channel is thin.
questions: Who are the main memory module makers and channel distributors, and how large are they?
What share of DRAM/NAND passes through the spot/channel market versus direct contracts?
How did the 2025-26 memory price rise pass through to PC, smartphone and server bill-of-materials costs and prices?
How reliable are spot-price series as leading indicators of contract prices?
primary_sources: ADATA and other listed module makers' annual reports (TWSE)
PC OEM 10-K commentary on memory costs (HP, Dell, Lenovo)
